meta.description: Polls the portal for approved, scheduled reels whose posting time has arrived, publishes them to Instagram via the Meta Graph API, reports the outcome back, and notifies the client by email and WhatsApp. All credentials come from n8n environment variables; no secrets live in this file.

parameters.content:
## Instagram Auto-Publisher

**What it does**
Every 5 minutes: ask the portal what is due, claim it, push it to Instagram, report back, tell the client.

**Why the portal decides, not this workflow**
n8n can run two executions at once. If this workflow decided what was due, both would pick the same reel and post it twice. `/publish/claim` settles that in the database — exactly one execution wins.

**The client's message goes through our own WhatsApp service**
Not Meta's Cloud API: that bills per business-initiated conversation and needs an approved template. whatsapp-service drives the agency's own account and costs nothing. The claim hands over `wa_chat_id` ready to use — the client's approval group when they have one, their number otherwise.

**Required environment variables**
- `PORTAL_URL` — https://nvkhub.vercel.app
- `PORTAL_API_KEY` — matches N8N_API_KEY in the portal
- `META_ACCESS_TOKEN` — long-lived page token, with instagram_content_publish
- `META_API_VERSION` — e.g. v21.0
- `WHATSAPP_SERVICE_URL` — http://whatsapp-service:4000 when both run in the same compose
- `WHATSAPP_SERVICE_TOKEN` — matches SERVICE_API_KEY in whatsapp-service

Set `N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE=false` so `$env` resolves.

### 1 · Find work

The queue is read-only. Nothing is reserved until the claim below, so a crashed run here costs nothing.

### 2 · Claim it

The concurrency guard. `ok:false` here is normal — another run got there first, or it is already live. Skip and move on; never fail the run.

### 3 · Publish via Meta Graph API

Instagram publishing is two steps and a wait:
1. **Create a container** — hands Meta the video URL. Returns immediately; Meta downloads and encodes in the background.
2. **Poll `status_code`** until `FINISHED`. Publishing a container that is still `IN_PROGRESS` fails.
3. **Publish** the finished container.

A 60-second reel typically finishes in 30–90s. The loop gives it up to 6 minutes.

### 4 · Report back & notify

The portal stores the media id, permalink and timestamp, then the client hears about it.

Notifications never fail the run: a client not getting a WhatsApp is a problem, but it is not a reason to mark a live post as failed.

### 5 · Failure path

Everything that can fail routes here. The portal decides whether to retry:

- attempts left → back to `scheduled`, the next poll picks it up
- budget spent → `failed`, and an admin is notified
- Meta code 190/200/9007 → permanent, no retries at all

That decision lives in the database on purpose. Re-importing this workflow can't change it.

nodes.name: Every 5 minutes
nodes.notes: Polling beats a webhook here: a post is due at a wall-clock time, and a webhook fired at approval time would need its own scheduler anyway. 5 minutes is the worst-case lateness a post can suffer.

nodes.name: Fetch publish queue
nodes.notes: GET /api/automation/publish/queue — approved + scheduled + time reached + client opted in. Returns { ok, count, items[] }. Each item already carries a fetchable video URL (signed if the R2 bucket is private) and the caption with hashtags appended, so no further lookups are needed.

nodes.name: Split queue into items
nodes.notes: Fans the items[] array out into n8n items and stamps a shared run id so every log line from this execution can be correlated.

nodes.name: Anything due?
nodes.notes: Nothing due is the normal case — most of the 288 runs a day end here. The false branch stops quietly rather than logging noise.

nodes.name: Nothing to post
nodes.notes: Deliberate dead end. An empty queue is success, not an error.

nodes.name: Post one at a time
nodes.notes: One post per iteration, on purpose. Publishing is stateful (claim → container → poll → publish) and each post waits on Meta's encoder; running them in parallel would interleave the waits and make a failure impossible to attribute. Output 0 = done, output 1 = next item.

nodes.name: Claim the deliverable
nodes.notes: The concurrency guard. Answers 409/410 when another run holds the item or it is already live — neverError:true keeps those as data so the IF below can skip cleanly instead of failing the whole batch. Moves the row to 'processing' and spends one attempt from its retry budget.

nodes.name: Claim won?
nodes.notes: Lost the race, already posted, or out of retries — all three mean 'not ours to publish'. Skip to the next item without touching the Graph API.

nodes.name: Skip (claimed elsewhere)
nodes.notes: Not a failure. Loops straight back for the next item.

nodes.name: Build Graph API request
nodes.notes: Chooses REELS vs IMAGE, picks the per-client token over the agency one, and fails fast with a readable message when either the token or the media URL is missing.

nodes.name: Create media container
nodes.notes: POST /{ig-user-id}/media. Returns { id } — the container, not a published post. Retried 3× in-node for transient 5xx/network blips; anything that survives that goes to the failure path where the portal decides about a later retry.

nodes.name: Container created?
nodes.notes: A Graph error body has no `id`. Most failures land here: expired token, unreachable media URL, account not eligible.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ deliverable_id: $('Build Graph API request').item.json.deliverable_id, stage: 'container_created', status: 'processing', container_id: $json.id, run_id: $('Build Graph API request').item.json.run_id }) }}

nodes.name: Log container created
nodes.notes: Breadcrumb only. neverError + continue: a logging failure must never take down a publish that is otherwise going fine.

nodes.name: Wait for encoding
nodes.notes: Meta downloads and transcodes the video before the container is publishable. Polling instantly always returns IN_PROGRESS, so wait first, then check — 30s covers most reels on the first pass.

parameters.url: =https://graph.facebook.com/{{ $('Build Graph API request').item.json.api_version }}/{{ $('Create media container').item.json.id }}?fields=status_code,status&access_token={{ $('Build Graph API request').item.json.access_token }}

nodes.name: Check container status
nodes.notes: GET /{container-id}?fields=status_code. FINISHED = publishable, IN_PROGRESS = still encoding, ERROR/EXPIRED = give up. Publishing an IN_PROGRESS container fails, which is why this poll exists at all.

nodes.name: Interpret status
nodes.notes: Turns the container status into ready / waiting / failed / timeout, and carries the poll counter that stops the wait loop running for ever.

nodes.name: Encoding finished?
nodes.notes: True → publish. False → still waiting, or out of patience (sorted by the next node).

nodes.name: Still encoding?
nodes.notes: True → back to Wait for another 30 seconds. False → the container errored or timed out; report the failure.

nodes.name: Publish to Instagram
nodes.notes: POST /{ig-user-id}/media_publish. The post goes live here. Returns { id } = the published media id. Only 2 tries: this is the one call that has a visible side effect, and a retry after an ambiguous timeout risks a duplicate post — the portal's idempotent markPosted is the backstop.

nodes.name: Published?
nodes.notes: A published media id, or a Graph error body.

nodes.name: Fetch permalink
nodes.notes: The publish response only returns an id. The permalink is what the client actually wants in their WhatsApp message, so it costs one extra call. Optional: if this fails the post is still live and the id alone is reported.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ deliverable_id: $('Interpret status').item.json.deliverable_id, status: 'posted', media_id: $('Publish to Instagram').item.json.id, permalink: $json.permalink || null, posted_at: $json.timestamp || new Date().toISOString(), run_id: $('Interpret status').item.json.run_id, duration_ms: Date.now() - $('Interpret status').item.json.publish_started_at }) }}

nodes.name: Report success
nodes.notes: Stores media id, permalink and publish timestamp; flips the deliverable to 'posted'. Retried hard (5×) — the post is already live, so failing to record it would leave the portal thinking it still needs publishing. The endpoint is idempotent, so retrying is safe.

nodes.name: Email the client
nodes.notes: The portal sends this, not n8n — it owns the branded template, the SMTP config and the client's address. Passing only the deliverable id means the workflow can't misaddress a client's mail.

nodes.name: WhatsApp the client
nodes.notes: Sends the 'your post is live' message through the agency's own WhatsApp service (whatsapp-web.js), not Meta's Cloud API: no per-message billing and no template approval. wa_chat_id comes from the claim and is already a usable chat id — the client's approval group when they have one, their number otherwise. Never errors the run: a post that went live is still a success even if the client wasn't told.

nodes.name: Next item
nodes.notes: Joins the branches back together and returns to the loop for the next post.

nodes.name: Normalise the failure
nodes.notes: Collapses four different failure shapes into one payload, pulling out Meta's numeric error code — the portal uses it to tell a retryable failure from a permanent one.

nodes.name: Report failure
nodes.notes: Releases the claim and lets the portal decide: back to 'scheduled' for another attempt, or 'failed' with an admin notification. Reporting the failure matters as much as reporting success — without it the row stays claimed until its lease expires.

nodes.name: On workflow crash
nodes.notes: Catches anything the branches above missed — a Code node throwing, n8n running out of memory. Without this a crashed execution is silent and the deliverable sits claimed until its 20-minute lease expires.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ deliverable_id: $json.execution?.lastNodeExecuted ? 0 : 0, stage: 'workflow_error', status: 'failed', error_message: `${$json.workflow?.name || 'Publisher'} crashed at node "${$json.execution?.lastNodeExecuted || 'unknown'}": ${$json.execution?.error?.message || 'unknown error'}`, run_id: `n8n-${$json.execution?.id || 'unknown'}` }) }}

nodes.name: Log the crash
nodes.notes: Best-effort record of a crashed execution. The lease on any claimed deliverable expires by itself after 20 minutes, so the queue recovers without intervention — this is the trail that explains why a post went out late.
